transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Any time I have to deal with those stronger cleaning chemicals, I either go out of my way to avoid them or push through it while feeling like I can’t stand being there. It's really starting to affect my job, so I knew I needed to come in and get some help.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happens when you're exposed to those stronger cleaning chemicals, such as any physical sensations or thoughts that you experience?

Just seeing a hazard symbol on a bottle makes my stomach drop, and if I smell the chemicals, my heart starts pounding and my hands get sweaty. I feel like I can't catch my breath, and I start shaking so badly that I feel like I might pass out or just need to bolt out the door.
Do you experience these intense physical and emotional reactions in response to other specific objects, situations, or events beyond just the stronger cleaning chemicals?

No, it's strictly limited to those stronger chemicals, their smells, and the supply closets where they are kept. I don't feel this way around any other objects, animals, or situations at all. The only other thing is that lately, I've even started avoiding some of my basic household cleaners at home.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by avoiding some of your basic household cleaners at home, and have you noticed any significant distress or impairment in your daily life due to this avoidance?

At home, I've stopped using regular bleach and strong disinfectants, switching to mild soaps or just skipping deep cleaning entirely because the smell panics me. At work, it has cost me a lot of money because I've turned down higher-paying routes and cut my hours to avoid those environments. Now, my supervisor has warned me that my job is on the line if I keep refusing to work with the standard chemicals.

Can you describe how you feel when you're in a situation where you know the strong cleaning chemicals are present but not directly visible or smelled, such as being in a room where you know they are stored but can't see or smell them?

Just knowing those chemicals are stored behind a door or in a closet is enough to trigger my anxiety, even if I can't see or smell them yet. My heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can't get a full breath before I've even touched the door handle.

Do you experience anxiety or avoidance behaviors when you think about or are reminded of the stronger cleaning chemicals when you're not in a situation where they're present, such as when you're at home and someone mentions them or you see a picture of a chemical bottle?

Yes, even when I'm not at work, just seeing a hazard symbol on a bottle or thinking about having to deal with them makes my stomach drop and my heart race. It's actually gotten to the point where I avoid using basic, ordinary cleaners at home because the mere thought of them triggers that same intense fear.

Can you tell me if there's anything specific about the stronger cleaning chemicals, such as their smell, appearance, or the hazard symbols on their labels, that you think triggers your intense fear and anxiety responses?

Yes, both the visual cues and the smells are major triggers for me. Just seeing a big drum or jug with a hazard symbol on it immediately makes my stomach drop with fear. If I catch even a hint of a chemical smell, it makes my physical symptoms, like my pounding heart and shortness of breath, ten times worse.
Do you fear the stronger cleaning chemicals themselves, or is your fear more focused on the potential harm or danger they might pose to you or others?

It started because of that scary time I was overwhelmed by fumes and taken to the ER, but now I fear the chemicals themselves. Just seeing a hazard symbol or catching a chemical scent triggers instant panic and a pounding heart, even though I know logically they are standard cleaners that others use safely. It's like my body just reacts with pure fear to the chemicals themselves now, regardless of the actual danger.
